claim: A critic rule that counts sectors measures the wrong thing: a 1,008-square-body courtyard was called 'circulation' because six tiny stair steps outnumbered it. Weigh by floor area, express scale as a percentile among corpus sectors of comparable footprint (never a round multiple of the body), never count a skipped evaluator as a pass, and cross-check a new rule against a rendered frame before trusting it.
evidence: First authoring-loop pilot, 2026-08-21: three iterations passed every gate while the level was an axis-aligned grid in the bottom decile for ceiling height.
use: Area-weighted measures and corpus percentiles; no aggregate quality score.
